text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

HET FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD - Dutch managers broadly support idea of public safety net, but strongly favour further individualisation within their own companies - survey. (p1) - Government watchdog says economic affairs ministry's rescue operations for large Dutch companies since 1987 have been poorly coordinated. (p1) - Retail group De Boer Winkelbedrijven is to merge its operations with Unigro. (p1) - Technical wholesaler Econosto takes over Van der Beyl Beheer. (p3) - Property fund Uni-Invest seeks to take over bourse-listed realty funds to realise its growth strategy. (p3) - Computer group LCI expands into Belgium with takeover of Prodata systems. (p5) - British food concern Grand Met is said to consider making an offer for food and beverages group BolsWessanen. (p5) - Financial services group ING unit Postbank to provide its customers hard and software for Internet banking. (p5)

DE VOLKSKRANT - Robeco to launch 13 country funds in November. (p2) - Some 75 jobs at storage and transport Pakhoed's unit Paktank threatened. (p2) - Dutch central bank president Wim Duisenberg optimistic about Germany meeting EMU-criteria. (p2) - Dutch transport association TLN submits complaint to European Commission against intended takeover of TNT by PTT Post. (p33)

DE TELEGRAAF - Row between cabinet and government watchdog about damning research into subsidies for Fokker, DAF and NedCar. (p1) - Unique finding in Leiden of golden mask from Roman period. (p1) - November 1 as deadline for Fokker takeover seems flexible for its suppliers. (p35) - Unions against growing practice of managers hiring "Mystery Guests" to improve quality of their staff. (p39)
TROUW - U.S. bus company Vancom threatens to leave the Netherlands, if government does not make haste with introducing more rivalry in public transport. (p1)

ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD - Airline companies fear aviation crisis due to high kerosene prices. (p12) - Businesses in the Netherlands optimistic about fourth quarter outlook. (p13) --Amsterdam newsdesk +31-20-504-5000
